title: Cross-language SDK: streaming auth renewal, rotation automation, and retry ergonomics
creator: Diego Martinez
description: Deliver concrete SDK patterns and implementations across Python, TypeScript, and Go for: (1) mid-stream auth renewal for long-lived streaming responses, (2) safe API key rotation and automated renewal with minimal request disruption, and (3) unified retry/backoff semantics for auth-related transient failures. Provide examples, test harnesses, and migration guidance for enterprise SSO token flows and local developer ergonomics.
acceptance_criteria: Language SDKs expose a consistent auth abstraction (TokenProvider interface) across Python/TS/Go
Streaming clients can transparently refresh credentials mid-stream without dropping partial data for >95% of test cases
Automated rotation helper supports dual-key rollover and recommended default polling intervals in all SDKs
Retry behavior for auth errors documented and implemented: exponential backoff with jitter, max retries configurable, immediate retry for token-refresh success
End-to-end examples added to examples/ with Python/TS/Go demos showing local dev SSO flow and enterprise token exchange
Unit and integration tests cover simulated key revocation, token expiry during streaming, and network partitions
tasks: Design TokenProvider abstraction and language idioms
Prototype mid-stream renewal approach for HTTP streaming (gRPC/http2/Server-Sent Events) — PoC in Python
Implement renewal + fallback policy in TypeScript SDK streaming client
Add key-rotation helpers: dual-key active/passive + auto-swap guidance
Integrate retry/backoff logic with existing SDK retry middleware
Write comprehensive examples and CI integration tests
Security review and threat model walkthrough
Prepare migration docs & deprecation plan for legacy auth flows
notes: 2026-01-20: Kickoff meeting — agreed on TokenProvider abstraction and language-specific adapter pattern. Diego to own design doc. Priya to lead implementation across SDKs.

2026-01-28: PoC (Python) shows streaming renewal can attach a new Authorization header via chunked metadata update on http2 and gRPC; SSE requires client reconnection in current browsers — short-term approach: transparent reconnection with resume token delivered by server.

2026-02-05: Trade-off: full zero-disruption for browser-based SSE is infeasible without server protocol changes; decision made to implement automatic reconnect with at-most-once/at-least-once semantics documented and opt-in resume tokens for users who want stronger guarantees.

2026-02-19: Added key-rotation helper API design: rotate_keys(active_key, new_key) with optional grace_period_seconds; SDKs will poll a rotation endpoint or accept pushed rotation via websocket for enterprise private deployments.
2026-02-27: Security review kickoff — initial threat model raised: replay attacks during token swap, race on dual-key swap, leakage in local env files. Listed mitigations in design doc.
2026-03-03: TypeScript streaming client PR implements TokenProvider + refresh hook; added exponential backoff with decorrelated jitter for auth failures. Integration tests pending.

2026-03-09: Go SDK PoC for token renewal uses context-aware token fetcher; observed edge case where long-running generator goroutine blocked on token refresh under 100ms pause — added non-blocking refresh with buffered channel to avoid head-of-line blocking.

2026-03-10: Drafted examples for local dev: 'redwood login' CLI flow to obtain enterprise SSO short-lived token, and an 'env merge' helper that stores secrets in OS keyrings for macOS/Linux/Windows. Added guidance to avoid checking .env files into repos.
comments: Priya Nair (2026-02-02): Request to prioritize browser compat for TS SDK — but agreed to surface limitations clearly and provide opt-in resume tokens.
Ava Chen (Security, 2026-02-27): Please ensure PKCE and state checks for SSO flows; avoid long-lived refresh tokens by default.
Liam OConnor (Platform, 2026-03-01): For Dedicated/Private customers we should provide webhook push for rotation events vs polling. Add to implementation backlog.
Diego Martinez (2026-03-07): Noted flaky test in Python CI when simulating network partition; increasing timeouts and adding deterministic token expiry in test harness.
Priya Nair (2026-03-10): Ready for initial security review; requesting reviewers in next sprint cycle.
migration_notes: Legacy SDK users using static API keys will continue to work; recommend migration path to ephemeral token with TokenProvider to reduce blast radius of key leaks.
Provide an automated migration script that can swap in TokenProvider with minimal code changes for common patterns (requests/axios/fetch/urllib).
Deprecate plain environment-file-only guidance in favor of OS keyring / credential helper + CI secret store references
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: Token refresh failure mid-stream can drop user-visible responses. Mitigation: implement automatic reconnect with resume tokens + configurable retry thresholds.
Risk: Key rotation race may allow short window of invalid credentials. Mitigation: dual-key rollover pattern + grace period and server-side acceptance of both keys for grace window.
Risk: Local developer secrets leaking in dotfiles. Mitigation: ship credential helper and strong docs for gitignore and keyring usage.
